proposals.before: After Emperor Zhenzong came to the throne in the Chongxi era, peace was made with the Khitan and the empire knew no major disturbances. He then carried out the feng rites on Mount Tai and sacrifices at Fenyin, while cults devoted to the Heavenly Writ and the Sage Ancestor rose one after another. A special office for detailed ritual determination was set up, and chief ministers, Hanlin scholars, and ritual officials were appointed to oversee it jointly.
proposals.after: After Emperor Zhenzong succeeded to an age of successive prosperity, peace was made with the Khitan and the empire knew no major disturbances. He then carried out the feng rites on Mount Tai and sacrifices at Fenyin, while cults devoted to the Heavenly Writ and the Sage Ancestor rose one after another. A special office for detailed ritual determination was set up, and chief ministers, Hanlin scholars, and ritual officials were appointed to oversee it jointly.
proposals.reason: 重熙之後 is the classical idiom for succeeding to successive prosperity/brilliance, not the Liao reign name Chongxi (which began after Zhenzong's death).

proposals.before: Emperor Zhenzong, after succeeding in the Chongxi era, once the Khitan had made peace and the realm was untroubled, thereupon performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai and sacrificed at Fenyin; veneration of the Heavenly Writ and the Sage Ancestor arose in succession, and a special Detailed Determination Office was established, with chief ministers, Hanlin academicians, and ritual officials ordered to take part in directing it.
proposals.after: Emperor Zhenzong, after succeeding to successive prosperity, once the Khitan had made peace and the realm was untroubled, thereupon performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai and sacrificed at Fenyin; veneration of the Heavenly Writ and the Sage Ancestor arose in succession, and a special Detailed Determination Office was established, with chief ministers, Hanlin academicians, and ritual officials ordered to take part in directing it.
proposals.reason: 重熙 is not the Liao Chongxi era here; it is the set phrase for an age of successive brilliance after which Zhenzong continued.

proposals.before: In the year after his accession, because Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctor Nie Chongyi submitted the Recompiled Diagrams of the Three Rites, an edict ordered Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Yin Zhuo to gather Confucian scholars to review them in detail.
proposals.after: In the year after his accession, because Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctor Nie Chongyi submitted the Recompiled Diagrams of the Three Rites, an edict ordered Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent Yin Zhuo to gather Confucian scholars to review them in detail.
proposals.reason: 太子詹事 is Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not Grand Mentor (太子太傅).

proposals.before: In the year after his accession, because Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctor Nie Chongyi submitted the Recompiled Diagrams of the Three Rites, an edict ordered Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Yin Zhuo to gather Confucian scholars to determine them in detail.
proposals.after: In the year after his accession, because Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctor Nie Chongyi submitted the Recompiled Diagrams of the Three Rites, an edict ordered Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent Yin Zhuo to gather Confucian scholars to determine them in detail.
proposals.reason: 太子詹事 should not be rendered Grand Mentor; that office is 太子太傅.

proposals.before: During Kaibao, as the four quarters gradually settled and the people gained some respite, Censor-in-Chief Liu Wensou, Secretariat Drafter Li Fang, Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Drafting Edict Officer Lu Duoxun, Vice Director of the Left Secretariat Office and Drafting Edict Officer Hu Meng, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Yang Zhaojian, Left Supplementation Aide Jia Huangzhong, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel He Xian, and Heir Apparent Attendant Chen E were ordered to compile the Kaibao Comprehensive Rites in two hundred juan, based on the Tang Kaiyuan Rites with additions and subtractions.
proposals.after: During Kaibao, as the four quarters gradually settled and the people gained some respite, Censor-in-Chief Liu Wensou, Secretariat Drafter Li Fang, Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Drafting Edict Officer Lu Duoxun, Vice Director of the Left Secretariat Office and Drafting Edict Officer Hu Meng, Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent Yang Zhaojian, Left Supplementation Aide Jia Huangzhong, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel He Xian, and Heir Apparent Attendant Chen E were ordered to compile the Kaibao Comprehensive Rites in two hundred juan, based on the Tang Kaiyuan Rites with additions and subtractions.
proposals.reason: Same office error: 太子詹事 is not Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

proposals.before: Before long, Song Minqiu, Hanlin academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, was also ordered, together with the Censorate, the Gate Office, and the Ritual Court, to determine in detail the Court Assembly Ceremonial Protocols, altogether forty-six juan: entitled Gate Office Protocols, Court Assembly Ritual Texts, Ceremonial Protocols, and Protocols for Honorific Titles and Imperial Registers.
proposals.after: Before long, Song Minqiu, academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, was also ordered, together with the Censorate, the Gate Office, and the Ritual Court, to determine in detail the Court Assembly Ceremonial Protocols, altogether forty-six juan: entitled Gate Office Protocols, Court Assembly Ritual Texts, Ceremonial Protocols, and Protocols for Honorific Titles and Imperial Registers.
proposals.reason: 龍圖直學士 is Dragon Diagram Hall Direct Academician, not a Hanlin academician; the literal line invents 'Hanlin'.

proposals.before: changing the Longevity Star sacrifice to worship of the Old Man of the South Pole;
proposals.after: changing the Longevity Star sacrifice to worship of the Old Man
proposals.reason: Chinese has only 老人; 'of the South Pole' is an interpretive addition not present in the source phrase.

proposals.before: Under Yuanyou the empress was invested; under Zhenghe the crown prince received his capping; under Yuanfu the western Jingling Palace was founded; under Chongning the emperor personally sacrificed at the Square Pond, built the Bright Hall, established the nine temples, cast the nine tripods, and sacrificed to Mars; under Daguan the Eight Treasures were received, and for all great sacrifices a ten-day period of abstention was required in advance.
proposals.after: Under Yuanyou the empress was invested; under Zhenghe the imperial prince received his capping; under Yuanfu the western Jingling Palace was founded; under Chongning the emperor personally sacrificed at the Square Pond, built the Bright Hall, established the nine temples, cast the nine tripods, and sacrificed to Mars; under Daguan the Eight Treasures were received, and for all great sacrifices a ten-day period of abstention was required in advance.
proposals.reason: Chinese 皇子 is 'imperial prince/son', not specifically the heir-apparent 太子; 'crown prince' over-specifies the rank.

proposals.before: As peace endured and classical learning flourished, scholars such as Wang Pu and Dong Bi became renowned authorities on ritual.
proposals.after: As peace endured and classical learning flourished, scholars such as Wang Pu and Dong Bian became renowned authorities on ritual.
proposals.reason: The corrupted glyph 董{分廾} is 董弁; pinyin is Bian, not Bi.

proposals.before: As peace lasted long and classical learning flourished brightly, scholars such as Wang Pu, Dong Bi, and others became famous specialists in ritual.
proposals.after: As peace lasted long and classical learning flourished brightly, scholars such as Wang Pu, Dong Bian, and others became famous specialists in ritual.
proposals.reason: The corrupted glyph 董{分廾} is 董弁; pinyin is Bian, not Bi.

proposals.before: the great la sacrifice was divided into four, with the eastern and western la pairing the sun with the moon;
proposals.after: the great la sacrifice was increased to four, with the eastern and western la taking the sun as principal and the moon as correlate;
proposals.reason: Chinese 增大蠟為四 means the great la was increased to four, not divided; 主日配月 makes the sun principal (主) and the moon the correlate (配), which the literal already captures.

proposals.before: Although minor sacrifices cannot all be performed, such as Heaven and Earth, the Five Thearchs, sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and the altars of soil and grain—I wish that the responsible offices be ordered to perform them on schedule.
proposals.after: Although minor sacrifices cannot all be performed, for such as Heaven and Earth, the Five Thearchs, the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and the altars of soil and grain, I wish that the responsible offices be ordered to perform them on schedule.
proposals.reason: The literal attaches 'such as' to the minor-sacrifices clause, reversing the sense: 如天地… lists the major rites Han wants restored despite not yet restoring all minor ones.

proposals.before: There are thirty great annual sacrifices: on the first xin day of the first month, prayer for grain; in early summer, the rain prayer; in late autumn, the great offering in the Bright Hall; at the winter solstice, sacrifice at the Circular Mound to August Heaven; on the first xin day of the first month, sacrifice to the Life-Generating Thearch; at the four seasonal establishments and on earth-sovereign days, sacrifice to the Five Directional Thearchs; at the spring equinox, the morning rite to the sun; at the autumn equinox, the evening rite to the moon; eastern and western Grand Unity; on the la day, the great year-end sacrifice to the hundred spirits; at the summer solstice, sacrifice to August Earth; in early winter, sacrifice to the Earth of the Divine Land; in the four first months of the seasons and in late winter, offerings at the Grand Temple and Rear Temple; in the two mid-seasons of spring and autumn and on the la day, sacrifice at the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain; and in the two mid-seasons, the Nine Palaces Noble Spirit.
proposals.after: There are thirty great annual sacrifices: on the first xin day of the first month, prayer for grain; in early summer, the rain prayer; in late autumn, the great offering in the Bright Hall; at the winter solstice, sacrifice at the Circular Mound to August Heaven Thearch; on the first xin day of the first month, sacrifice to the Life-Generating Thearch; at the four seasonal establishments and on earth-sovereign days, sacrifice to the Five Directional Thearchs; at the spring equinox, the morning rite to the sun; at the autumn equinox, the evening rite to the moon; eastern and western Grand Unity; on the la day, the great year-end sacrifice to the hundred spirits; at the summer solstice, sacrifice to August Earth; in early winter, sacrifice to the Earth of the Divine Land; in the four first months of the seasons and in late winter, offerings at the Grand Temple and Rear Temple; in the two mid-seasons of spring and autumn and on the la day, sacrifice at the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain; and in the two mid-seasons, the Nine Palaces Noble Spirit.
proposals.reason: Chinese 昊天上帝 is August Heaven Thearch; the idiomatic drops 上帝/Thearch while the literal correctly keeps it.

proposals.before: It was now argued that the Three Excellencies of Grand Commandant were not appropriate to this duty and that the minister of personnel should preside over abstention.
proposals.after: It was now argued that the Grand Commandant, being among the Three Excellencies, was not suited to this duty and that the minister of personnel should preside over abstention.
proposals.reason: 太尉三公 means the Grand Commandant as one of the Three Excellencies, not a body called the Three Excellencies of Grand Commandant.

proposals.before: He also said: 'Earlier scholars held that sacrifices offered on solid firewood altars required no jade, and those offered by Zheng and You burning required no silks.
proposals.after: He also said: 'Earlier scholars held that sacrifices offered on solid firewood altars required no jade, and those offered by the kuai-you burning rite required no silks.
proposals.reason: 郐鍮燎 names a ritual burning category, not persons or places Zheng and You.

proposals.before: He also said: 'Former scholars held that those sacrificed to by solid firewood had no jade, and those sacrificed to by Zheng and You burning had no silks.
proposals.after: He also said: 'Former scholars held that those sacrificed to by solid firewood had no jade, and those sacrificed to by kuai-you burning had no silks.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 郐鍮燎 is a rite type, not the names Zheng and You.

proposals.before: The claim that Zheng and You burning required no silks may also be incorrect.'
proposals.after: The claim that kuai-you burning required no silks may also be incorrect.'
proposals.reason: Continues the s0138 mistranslation of 郐鍮燎 as personal or place names.

proposals.before: That Zheng and You burning had no silks may perhaps not be so.'
proposals.after: That kuai-you burning had no silks may perhaps not be so.'
proposals.reason: Same ritual-term mistranslation of 郐鍮燎 in the literal rendering.

proposals.before: In the third year of Qingli, ritual official Yu Jing said: 'Prayer for grain and sacrifice to the Life-Generating Thearch fall on the same day; their rites should differ and cannot all use four gui with base; color should favor red.'
proposals.after: In the third year of Qingli, ritual official Yu Jing said: 'Prayer for grain and sacrifice to the Life-Generating Thearch fall on the same day; their rites should differ and cannot all use four gui with base, with red as the favored color.'
proposals.reason: 色尚赤 continues the rejected shared practice with 四圭有邸; the literal wrongly makes favoring red a separate imperative.

proposals.before: The tray order is shoulder, arm, shank, main spine, thigh spine, cross spine, substitute rib, long rib, short rib, rib-flap, and shank-flap—eleven parts; bone parts are presented before the spirit seat as in the Lesser Penance rite, all lower end first.
proposals.after: The tray order is shoulder, arm, shank, main spine, thigh spine, cross spine, substitute rib, long rib, short rib, rib-flap, and shank-flap—eleven parts; bone parts are presented before the spirit seat as in the Lesser Victims (shaolao) rite, all lower end first.
proposals.reason: 少牢 denotes the lesser animal sacrifice of sheep and pig, not a penance rite.

proposals.before: The order on the tray is shoulder, arm, shank, main spine, thigh spine, cross spine, substitute rib, long rib, short rib, rib-flap, and shank-flap—eleven parts in all; when bone parts ascend the tray they are presented before the spirit seat as in the Lesser Penance rite, all presented lower end first.
proposals.after: The order on the tray is shoulder, arm, shank, main spine, thigh spine, cross spine, substitute rib, long rib, short rib, rib-flap, and shank-flap—eleven parts in all; when bone parts ascend the tray they are presented before the spirit seat as in the Lesser Victims (shaolao) rite, all presented lower end first.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 少牢禮 as penance rather than the lesser sacrificial victims rite.

decisions.reason: 承重熙之後 is the classical idiom for succeeding to successive prosperity; Chongxi is a Liao era that began after Zhenzong's death and cannot date his accession.
In the literal, 重熙 likewise names successive brilliance, not the Liao Chongxi era.
太子詹事 is Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent; Grand Mentor is 太子太傅.
The literal must also render 太子詹事 as Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not Grand Mentor.
For 楊昭儉 the same office 太子詹事 is not Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
龍圖直學士 does not include Hanlin; the literal invents that affiliation.

decisions.after: changing the Longevity Star sacrifice to worship of the Old Man;
decisions.reason: Chinese has only 老人; 'of the South Pole' is invented, but the list item should keep the closing semicolon.
皇子 is an imperial prince/son, not specifically the heir-apparent 太子; crown prince over-specifies.
